name: AC ChievoVerona
content:
AC ChievoVerona was an Italian football club from Chievo, a small district of Verona, founded in 1929. For most of its history it was an amateur neighbourhood team, playing in the regional leagues under various names. Its rise began in the 1980s and 1990s, when the club, backed by the Paluani bakery company, climbed through the lower divisions and reached Serie B in 1994. Chievo shared the Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi with its city rival Hellas Verona.

In 2001 Chievo won promotion to Serie A for the first time, and its debut season became one of the great fairy tales of Italian football: the "Flying Donkeys" led the table in the autumn and finished fifth, qualifying for the UEFA Cup. The club established itself as a regular top-flight side for almost two decades, and in 2006 it reached the qualifying round of the UEFA Champions League after the Calciopoli scandal reshaped the final Serie A standings.

After relegation in 2019, the club ran into serious financial difficulties. In 2021 it was excluded from Serie B over unpaid tax debts and ceased its professional activity. A new club claiming its heritage later restarted from the amateur leagues, but the original AC ChievoVerona remains remembered as one of the most remarkable small-club success stories in Italian football.

name: Málaga CF
content:
Málaga CF is a Spanish football club from Málaga, Andalusia, playing its home matches at La Rosaleda Stadium. The club traces its roots to CD Málaga, founded in 1904, but the current entity was established on 25 May 1948 as Club Atlético Malagueño, originally the reserve team of CD Málaga. After CD Málaga was dissolved in 1992 because of its debts, Atlético Malagueño took over as the city's main club and in 1994 changed its name to Málaga Club de Fútbol.

The renamed club climbed quickly through the divisions and reached La Liga in 1999. In 2002 it won the UEFA Intertoto Cup and went on to reach the quarter-finals of the 2002–03 UEFA Cup. After a spell in the second tier, Málaga returned to the top flight in 2008, and in 2010 the club was bought by Qatari businessman Abdullah bin Nasser Al Thani, whose investment brought in well-known players and coach Manuel Pellegrini.

The club's greatest success came in the 2012–13 season, its debut in the UEFA Champions League: Málaga topped a group with Milan and Zenit, knocked out Porto in the round of 16 and were eliminated by Borussia Dortmund in the quarter-finals only by two stoppage-time goals. Financial problems and UEFA sanctions followed, the club was relegated in 2018, and it was later placed under judicial administration, continuing to compete in the Spanish professional leagues.

names.name: Club Atlético Malagueño
names.note: Club founded under this name as the reserve team of CD Málaga

name: Panachaiki FC
content:
Panachaiki is a Greek football club from Patras, the largest city of the Peloponnese. Its parent sports club was founded on 14 June 1891 as Panachaikos Gymnastikos Syllogos, and in 1923 it merged with the rival Gymnastiki Etaireia Patron to form Panachaiki Gymnastiki Enosi. The football department dates back to 1899, when it played its first match against a team of British sailors. The club plays in red and black at the Kostas Davourlis Stadium, its traditional home ground.

Panachaiki's best era came in the 1970s, when it was a regular member of the Greek top flight. In 1973–74 it became the first Greek club from outside Athens and Thessaloniki to play in a European competition, knocking out Grazer AK in the first round of the UEFA Cup before losing to Twente. The club also reached the semi-finals of the Greek Cup in 1979 and 1997.

Since the late 1990s Panachaiki has spent most of its time in the lower divisions of Greek football, but it remains one of the oldest and best-supported clubs in the country, known as the Great Lady of the Peloponnese.

name: Wuppertaler SV
content:
Wuppertaler SV is a German football club from Wuppertal, North Rhine-Westphalia. It was formed on 8 July 1954 by the merger of TSG Vohwinkel and SSV Wuppertal, clubs whose roots go back to 1880 and 1904. The new club immediately won the second-division Oberliga West title and became one of the leading sides of the region, playing its home matches at the Stadion am Zoo.

In 1972 Wuppertal won the Regionalliga West and the promotion play-offs to reach the Bundesliga. Its debut season, 1972–73, was the best in the club's history: the newly promoted side spent weeks in second place and finished fourth, earning a place in the 1973–74 UEFA Cup, where it went out in the first round to Ruch Chorzów after a 5–4 home win. The club spent three seasons in the Bundesliga before relegation in 1975.

In 2004 the club merged with Borussia Wuppertal and played as Wuppertaler SV Borussia, returning to its original name in 2013 after financial difficulties. Today it competes in the regional leagues of German football.

names.name: Wuppertaler SV
names.note: Club founded under this name (merger of TSG Vohwinkel and SSV Wuppertal)

name: AC Cesena
content:
AC Cesena was an Italian football club from Cesena in Emilia-Romagna, founded in 1940. Playing in white and black at the Stadio Dino Manuzzi, the club rose through the lower divisions, reached Serie B in 1968 and won promotion to Serie A for the first time in 1973. With players such as Pierluigi Cera and Gianluigi Savoldi it quickly established itself in the top flight.

Cesena's best season came in 1975–76, when the club finished sixth in Serie A and qualified for the UEFA Cup. Its European debut in 1976–77 ended in the first round against 1. FC Magdeburg (0–3 away, 3–1 at home), and the side was relegated the following spring. The Seahorses later returned to Serie A several times, in 1981, 1987, 2010 and 2014, spending a total of thirteen seasons in the top division.

After years of financial difficulties the club went bankrupt and was dissolved in 2018. In the same year Romagna Centro was renamed Cesena FC and took over the identity and traditions of the old club.

name: Orduspor
content:
Orduspor is a Turkish football club from Ordu on the Black Sea coast, founded in 1967. It grew out of the city's mixed team, built around players from local clubs such as Karadeniz İdman Yurdu and Gençleryurdu, which finished second at the 1966 Turkish junior championship and persuaded the football federation to admit a professional side from Ordu. Playing in purple and white, the club made its home at the 19 Eylül Stadium in the city centre.

Orduspor's first golden era came in the late 1970s. After reaching the top division, the club qualified for the 1979–80 UEFA Cup, where it famously beat Baník Ostrava at home before being eliminated in the return leg. The club then moved between the first and second divisions for several seasons.

Orduspor returned to the Turkish Süper Lig in 2011 after a long absence but was relegated two years later. Financial problems followed and the club dropped into the lower leagues of Turkish football.

name: KFC Winterslag
content:
KFC Winterslag was a Belgian football club from Winterslag, a mining district of Genk in Limburg, founded in 1923 as Winterslag Football Club and registered with matricule number 322. Playing in red and black at De Noordlaan stadium, it was the club of the local coal miners, which gave it the nickname De Kolenputters. It became Koninklijke Football Club Winterslag in 1972.

The club's big rise came in the 1970s, when it climbed from the third division to the Belgian top flight, where it spent nine seasons in total. Its finest moment came in the 1981–82 UEFA Cup: Winterslag knocked out Bryne of Norway and then the famous Arsenal on away goals, before losing to Dundee United in the next round.

In 1988 Winterslag merged with its local rival Waterschei Thor to form KRC Genk, which kept Winterslag's matricule number 322 and went on to become one of the leading clubs in Belgium.

name: Portimonense SC
content:
Portimonense Sporting Clube is a Portuguese football club from Portimão, the second largest city of the Algarve, founded on 14 August 1914. Playing in black and white at the Estádio Municipal de Portimão, the club is the main sporting institution of the city and also fields teams in other sports such as basketball.

Portimonense enjoyed its best period in the 1980s, when it spent the whole decade in the Portuguese top flight. Its fifth-place finish in 1984–85, which included goalless home draws with Benfica and Sporting, earned the club its only European appearance in the 1985–86 UEFA Cup, where it was eliminated in the first round by Partizan. The club also reached the semi-finals of the Taça de Portugal in 1983, 1987 and 1988.

In the 1990s and 2000s Portimonense mostly played in the second tier. It returned to the Primeira Liga in 2010 and again in 2017 under coach Vítor Oliveira, and has since moved between the first and second divisions of Portuguese football.

name: BSG Stahl Brandenburg
content:
BSG Stahl Brandenburg is a German football club from Brandenburg an der Havel, founded on 20 November 1950 as BSG Einheit Brandenburg. In 1955 it took the name Stahl Brandenburg to reflect the backing of the town's steel works, whose support allowed the club to attract players from other East German teams and build a loyal following. The team plays at the Stadion Am Quenz.

Stahl reached the DDR-Oberliga in 1984 and stayed in the East German top flight until reunification. Its strong 1985–86 Oberliga season earned the club its only European campaign: in the 1986–87 UEFA Cup it knocked out Coleraine before losing to IFK Göteborg, the eventual winners.

After 1990 the club played as BSV Stahl Brandenburg, spending the 1991–92 season in the 2. Bundesliga. The closure of the steel mill cost it its main sponsor, and after bankruptcy in 1998 it re-formed as FC Stahl Brandenburg, playing in the lower leagues. In 2022 it returned to its historic name, BSG Stahl Brandenburg.

name: CSM Flacăra Moreni
content:
CSM Flacăra Moreni is a Romanian football club from Moreni in Dâmbovița County, founded in 1922 by English and Dutch engineers of the local oil refinery as Astra Română Moreni. It became Partizanul Moreni in 1950 and Flacăra Moreni a year later; after a merger with local rival Automecanica in 1977 it played as Flacăra Automecanica Moreni before returning to the name Flacăra Moreni in 1985. The club plays in yellow and blue at the Flacăra Stadium.

During the communist era the club enjoyed the backing of the Securitate and rose to the top flight in the 1980s. Its best season was 1988–89, when it finished fourth in the Divizia A and qualified for the UEFA Cup, where it lost to Porto in the first round of the 1989–90 competition.

After the fall of communism Flacăra lost its support and was relegated at the end of the 1989–90 season. Since then the club has played only in the lower divisions of Romanian football.

name: FC Wettingen
content:
FC Wettingen is a Swiss football club from Wettingen in the canton of Aargau, founded in 1931. For decades it played in the lower Swiss leagues before reaching the Nationalliga B in 1969 and spending a single season in the top flight in 1969–70. The club plays its home matches at the Stadion Altenburg.

Wettingen returned to the Nationalliga A in 1982 and, after a brief relegation, enjoyed the most successful season in its history in 1988–89, finishing fourth and qualifying for the UEFA Cup. In the 1989–90 competition it knocked out Dundalk before giving Napoli, the holders, a tough contest in the second round.

Financial problems led to the club's bankruptcy in 1993. It was refounded the same year as FC Wettingen 93 and in 2012 took back its original name, continuing in the regional leagues of Swiss football.

name: FK Rad
content:
FK Rad is a Serbian football club from Banjica, Belgrade, founded on 10 March 1958 by the construction company GP Rad, which took over the league rights of the small local club Razvitak. Known as the Builders, the club plays its home matches at the King Peter I Stadium.

Rad reached the Yugoslav Second League in 1973 and won promotion to the Yugoslav First League in 1987. In only its second top-flight season, 1988–89, it finished fourth and qualified for the UEFA Cup, where it was eliminated by Olympiacos in the first round of the 1989–90 competition.

After the breakup of Yugoslavia the club remained a regular member of the top division, with several top-five finishes around the turn of the millennium. In total it spent thirty seasons in the top flight between 1987 and 2021, before dropping into the lower leagues of Serbian football.

name: SC Salgueiros
content:
Sport Comércio e Salgueiros is a Portuguese multi-sports club from the parish of Paranhos in Porto, founded on 8 December 1911 as Sport Grupo e Salgueiros by a group of friends inspired by a match between Porto and Benfica. It chose red shirts to stand apart from its city rivals, became Sport Porto e Salgueiros in 1916–17 and, after joining forces with Sport Comércio in 1920, took its present name.

For decades Salgueiros was a mainstay of the Portuguese second division, with occasional seasons in the top flight. From the early 1980s it established itself in the Primeira Liga, and a strong 1990–91 league season earned the club its only European campaign, in the 1991–92 UEFA Cup, where it lost to Cannes on penalties in the first round. Its home was the Estádio Engenheiro Vidal Pinheiro.

In the 2000s the club fell into a deep financial crisis, lost its stadium and was administratively relegated in 2005. Salgueiros continues in the lower leagues of Portuguese football, playing at the Complexo Desportivo de Campanhã.

name: CD Tenerife
content:
Club Deportivo Tenerife is a Spanish football club from Santa Cruz de Tenerife in the Canary Islands, founded on 8 August 1922. Playing in white shirts and blue shorts at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López, the club spent its early decades in the regional leagues, reached the Segunda División in 1953 and made a brief first appearance in La Liga in 1961–62.

Under president Javier Pérez the club rose from the third tier to La Liga in 1989 and began a ten-year stay in the top flight. Coached by Jorge Valdano, Tenerife finished fifth in 1992–93 and reached the last 16 of the UEFA Cup the following season; under Jupp Heynckes it finished fifth again in 1995–96 and went on to the semi-finals of the 1996–97 UEFA Cup, beating Lazio, Feyenoord and Brøndby along the way.

Tenerife returned to La Liga for single seasons in 2001–02 and 2009–10 and has otherwise competed mostly in the Segunda División. Together with Las Palmas, with whom it contests the Canary Islands derby, it is one of the most geographically isolated professional clubs in Spain.

name: FC Tekstilshchik Kamyshin
content:
FC Tekstilshchik Kamyshin is a Russian football club from Kamyshin in Volgograd Oblast, founded in 1958 and named after the town's textile industry. It played in the Soviet Second League from 1988 and won promotion to the First League after the 1990 season, which entitled it to a place in the new Russian Top Division after the breakup of the Soviet Union. The team plays at the Tekstilshchik Stadium.

The club spent five seasons in the Russian top flight in the 1990s. Its best result was fourth place in 1993, which earned Tekstilshchik a place in the 1994–95 UEFA Cup, where it knocked out Békéscsaba of Hungary before losing to Nantes in the second round.

Two consecutive relegations in 1996 and 1997 began a long decline, and the club dropped into amateur football. Since 2009 it has competed in the Volgograd Oblast championship.

name: FC Volov Shumen
content:
FC Volov Shumen is a Bulgarian football club from Shumen, founded on 1 December 1929 as Panayot Volov, after a hero of the April Uprising. Thanks to the city's famous Shumensko beer, the team is known as the Brewers. It plays in yellow and blue at the Panayot Volov Stadium, which once held over 24,000 spectators.

The club took part in the national championship as Shumen regional champion in the 1930s, and later played as DFS Shumen, Madara Shumen and, from 1985, FC Shumen. Its best era came in the 1990s in the Bulgarian A Group: a fourth-place finish in 1993–94 brought its only European campaign, in the 1994–95 UEFA Cup, where it lost to Anorthosis Famagusta in the preliminary round.

The club later lost its sponsors and went bankrupt, folding its senior team in 2014 before being refounded in 2018. In 2024 it merged with Shumen 2007 to form Volov Shumen 2007, which plays in the third tier of Bulgarian football.

name: Trelleborgs FF
content:
Trelleborgs FF is a Swedish football club from Trelleborg in Skåne, founded on 6 December 1926. A modest provincial side making the most of limited resources, the club is known for its strong defences, good goalkeepers and a fine home record at Vångavallen, nicknamed Tjongavallen because of the team's long-ball style.

Trelleborg reached the Allsvenskan in 1984 and enjoyed its peak in the early 1990s, finishing third in 1992, its best ever result, and fourth in 1993. That earned the club its only European campaign: in the 1994–95 UEFA Cup it knocked out GI Gøta and then, famously, Blackburn Rovers, before losing to Lazio in the second round.

The club has played seventeen seasons in the Allsvenskan in total, most recently in 2018, and has otherwise competed in the Superettan and lower divisions of Swedish football.

name: SC Eendracht Aalst
content:
SC Eendracht Aalst was a Belgian football club from Aalst in East Flanders, founded on 25 June 1919 after local people had played charity matches for prisoners of war during the First World War. Known as the Onions, the club joined the national divisions in 1932 and first reached the top flight in 1939, playing its home matches at the Pierre Cornelis Stadium.

After decades in the lower divisions, including a relegation to the bottom national tier after a bribery affair in 1965, Aalst returned to the first division in 1994 under coach Jan Ceulemans, with players such as Godwin Okpara and Gilles De Bilde. A strong first season back earned the club a place in the 1995–96 UEFA Cup, where it knocked out Levski Sofia before losing to Roma in the second round.

The original club went into liquidation in 2002 and the team continued under a new licence from the third division. After years of licensing problems it dropped into the provincial leagues, and in February 2025 the club was declared bankrupt and folded.

name: OFK Bečej 1918
content:
OFK Bečej 1918 is a Serbian football club from Bečej in Vojvodina, founded in 1918. Nicknamed the Tisza's Ship after the river that runs through the town, the club plays at the Gradski stadion kraj Tise. It rose through the Vojvodina League and the Yugoslav Inter-Republic League at the end of the 1980s and won the final edition of the Yugoslav Second League in 1991–92, earning promotion to the top flight for the first time.

Bečej spent six seasons in the First League of FR Yugoslavia between 1992 and 1998. A fourth-place finish in 1994–95 took it to the 1995 Intertoto Cup, and another fourth place in 1995–96 earned a spot in the 1996–97 UEFA Cup, where it was eliminated by Mura in the preliminary round.

After relegation in 1998 the club slid down the divisions. It took the name OFK Bečej 1918 in 2012, won promotion back to the Serbian First League in 2018 and celebrated its centenary the same year.

name: Torpedo Rīga
content:
Torpedo Rīga was a Latvian football club from Riga, originally the team of the city's taxi park and known for decades as FK RTP (Riga Taxi Park). Its players combined football with work as taxi drivers. The club reached the Latvian Cup final in 1963 and earned a place in the Latvian league after the 1978 season, finishing fourth in its debut year.

Coached by Arkādijs Perkins, Torpedo won the Latvian championship in 1984 and 1986. After independence the club changed its name several times: it became Vidus Rīga in 1993, Amstrig Rīga in 1995 and Daugava Rīga in 1996. As Daugava it was runner-up in the Virslīga in 1996 and 1997, with striker Mihails Miholaps scoring 33 goals in 1996, and played in the UEFA Cup in 1997–98 and 1998–99.

Financial problems followed. Renamed LU/Daugava Rīga, the club gave up its top-flight place after 1998, won the first league in 1999, finished last in the 2000 Virslīga and then merged with Policijas FK to form PFK Daugava.

name: İstanbulspor
content:
İstanbulspor is a Turkish football club from Istanbul, founded on 4 January 1926 by students of Istanbul High School led by Kemal Halim Gürgen. One of the first sports clubs of the Republican era, it won both the Istanbul League and the Turkish Football Championship in 1931–32, the greatest success in its history. For decades it was regarded as Istanbul's fourth club after Beşiktaş, Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe.

Run by the Istanbul High School foundation until 1990, the club moved between the divisions and even dropped to amateur level. In 1990 it was bought by Cem Uzan's Uzan Holding, returned to the top flight in 1995 and finished fourth in 1997–98, earning a place in the 1998–99 UEFA Cup.

When the Uzan family withdrew its support in 2001 the club fell into financial crisis; it was taken over by the state in 2003 and relegated from the Süper Lig in 2005. İstanbulspor later returned to the top division in 2022, playing its home matches at the Necmi Kadıoğlu Stadium.

name: Rayo Vallecano
content:
Rayo Vallecano is a Spanish football club from the Puente de Vallecas district of Madrid, founded on 29 May 1924 as Agrupación Deportiva El Rayo. Proud of its working-class roots and neighbourhood identity, the club adopted its famous red diagonal stripe in 1949, inspired by River Plate, after an agreement with Atlético Madrid. Since 1976 it has played at the Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas.

Always in the shadow of Real Madrid and Atlético, Rayo became one of Spain's best-known yo-yo clubs, moving between La Liga and the Segunda División through the 1980s and 1990s. Its first European campaign came in the 2000–01 UEFA Cup, entered through the Fair Play ranking, when the club reached the quarter-finals before losing to Alavés.

Rayo has spent more than twenty seasons in the top flight, won the Segunda División in 2017–18 and returned to Europe in the 2025–26 Conference League. By historical record it is the third club of the Community of Madrid.
stadium: Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas, Cap. 14,708

name: ES Troyes AC
content:
Espérance Sportive Troyes Aube Champagne, known as ESTAC or simply Troyes, is a French football club from Troyes in the Champagne region, founded in 1986. It is the third professional club from the city after AS Troyes-Savinienne, which reached the 1956 Coupe de France final, and Troyes Aube Football. The team plays its home matches at the Stade de l'Aube.

Built up from the amateur leagues, ESTAC climbed rapidly through the divisions in the 1990s and reached Ligue 1 in 1999. In 2001 it won the UEFA Intertoto Cup, earning a place in the 2001–02 UEFA Cup, where it beat Ružomberok before going out to Leeds United in the second round.

Since then Troyes has moved between Ligue 1 and Ligue 2, winning the second division title several times. The club is now part of the City Football Group.

name: FC Chernomorets Novorossiysk
content:
FC Chernomorets Novorossiysk is the oldest Russian football club, founded in 1907 in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk as the football section of the Olympia sports club. Known as the Sailors, the club has played under several names: Tsement Novorossiysk in 1960–1969 and 1978–1991, Trud in the 1970s and Gekris in 1992–1993. It plays at the Central Stadium.

After decades in the lower Soviet leagues, Chernomorets won the Russian First Division in 1994 and spent seven seasons in the Top Division from 1995 to 2001. Its best results were sixth places in 1997 and 2000, the latter earning a place in the 2001–02 UEFA Cup, where it was knocked out by Valencia in the first round.

After relegation the club lost its professional licence in 2004 and restarted in the amateur league, briefly as FC Novorossiysk. It later returned to the professional divisions, winning promotion to the Russian First League in 2023.

name: Denizlispor
content:
Denizlispor is a Turkish sports club from Denizli in the Aegean region, founded on 26 May 1966 through the merger of two youth clubs, Çelik Yeşilspor Gençlik and Pamukkale Gençlik. Known for its green and black colours and nicknamed the Roosters, the club also runs volleyball, basketball and other sections. Its football team plays at the Denizli Atatürk Stadium.

Denizlispor's finest era came in the early 2000s in the Süper Lig. A fifth-place finish in 2001–02 brought its first European campaign: in the 2002–03 UEFA Cup the club knocked out Lorient, Sparta Prague and Lyon before losing in the fourth round to Porto, the eventual winners. It finished fifth again in 2003–04.

After relegation in 2010 the club spent nine seasons in the TFF First League, won it in 2018–19 and returned to the top flight for two seasons. It then suffered successive relegations into the lower divisions of Turkish football.

name: NK Kamen Ingrad
content:
NK Kamen Ingrad was a Croatian football club from Velika, a small town near Požega in Slavonia. It was founded in 1929 as NK Velika and renamed NK Papuk after the Second World War. In 1999 the local construction company Kamen Ingrad became its main sponsor and gave the club its name, playing its home matches at the Stadion Kamen Ingrad.

With the sponsor's backing the club rose quickly and reached the Prva HNL in 2002. It finished high enough to play in the 2003–04 UEFA Cup, where it beat Etzella Ettelbruck in the qualifying round before losing to Schalke 04 by a single goal in the first round.

The sponsor's financial troubles soon hit the team: Kamen Ingrad was relegated in 2007, dropped to the third tier in 2008 and ceased operations in July 2008. A new club, NK Papuk Velika, was formed afterwards, but it is legally a separate entity.

name: CD Nacional
content:
Clube Desportivo Nacional, known as Nacional da Madeira, is a Portuguese football club from Funchal on the island of Madeira, founded on 8 December 1910. Playing in black and white, it is a multi-sports club and contests the Madeira derby with Marítimo. Since 1998 its home has been the Estádio da Madeira, high in the Choupana district above Funchal.

Nacional first reached the Primeira Liga in 1988 and returned in 2002 under José Peseiro. Its best league finishes were fourth places in 2003–04 and 2008–09, the first of which earned the club its European debut in the 2004–05 UEFA Cup, where it lost to Sevilla in the first round. Over the following decade it played in Europe five times, famously knocking out Zenit Saint Petersburg in 2009.

The club spent fifteen consecutive seasons in the top flight from 2002 to 2017 and has since moved between the first and second divisions of Portuguese football.

name: Egaleo FC
content:
Egaleo is a Greek football club from Aigaleo, a suburb in the west of Athens. It traces its history to 1931, when Athlitiki Enosis Ieropoleos was founded, and in 1946 three local clubs merged with it to form Athlitikos Omilos Egaleo. The club first reached the Greek top flight in 1961 and finished fourth in 1970–71, its best ever season.

In 2003–04 Egaleo finished fifth and qualified for the UEFA Cup for the first time. In the 2004–05 competition it knocked out Gençlerbirliği to reach the group stage, where it faced Partizan, Lazio, Middlesbrough and Villarreal and collected one point. Its home matches that season were played at the Georgios Kamaras Stadium.

After relegation in 2007 the club dropped through the divisions, merged with Ilisiakos in 2009 and has since competed in the lower leagues, playing at the Stavros Mavrothalassitis Stadium.

name: FC Mariupol
content:
FC Mariupol was a Ukrainian football club from the Azov Sea port of Mariupol, founded in 1960 and long associated with the city's steelworks. From 2002 to 2017 it played as Illichivets Mariupol, the name under which it took part in European competitions, before being renamed FC Mariupol as part of Ukraine's decommunisation. Its home ground was the Volodymyr Boyko Stadium.

The club was a regular member of the Ukrainian Premier League. It made its European debut in the 2004–05 UEFA Cup, beating Urartu in the first qualifying round before losing to Austria Wien, and later played in the Europa League qualifiers as well.

The club ceased to compete in 2022, when its stadium and facilities were destroyed during the Russian siege of Mariupol. In 2023 the Brazilian club AA Batel adopted its name, colours and badge as a tribute.

name: 1. FSV Mainz 05
content:
1. FSV Mainz 05 is a German professional football club based in Mainz, the capital of Rhineland-Palatinate. It traces its origins to 1. Mainzer Fussballclub Hassia, founded on 16 March 1905, and after a series of mergers took its present name in 1919. The club plays its home matches at the Mewa Arena, which replaced the old Bruchwegstadion in 2011.

For most of its history Mainz was a regional and second-division side. Under coach Jürgen Klopp the club won promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2004, and in its first top-flight season it earned a place in the 2005–06 UEFA Cup through the UEFA Fair Play ranking, beating Mika and Keflavík before losing to Sevilla in the first round.

After a brief relegation, Mainz returned to the Bundesliga in 2009 and has since been an established member of the league, known for developing coaches such as Thomas Tuchel and for its carnival-flavoured identity. It has also taken part in the Europa League and the UEFA Conference League.

name: NK Žepče
content:
NK Žepče is a football club from the town of Žepče in central Bosnia and Herzegovina, founded in 1919 and today registered as NK Žepče 1919. Over its history the club changed its name several times and competed longest under the name Orlovik. Its home ground is the Žepče City Stadium, which holds around 4,000 spectators.

The club enjoyed its most successful period in the early 2000s. Playing as NK Zovko Žepče, it won the First League of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2001–02 and then spent six seasons, from 2002 to 2008, in the Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina; from 2003 it was known as Žepče Limorad after its main sponsor.

Žepče's only European campaign came in the 2005–06 UEFA Cup, where it met Bashkimi of Macedonia in the first qualifying round. The first leg was awarded 3–0 to Bashkimi because Žepče had fielded an ineligible player, and a 1–1 draw at home ended the tie. The club now plays in the lower tiers of Bosnian football.

name: FK Hajduk Kula
content:
FK Hajduk Kula was a Serbian football club from the town of Kula in Vojvodina, founded in 1925 as SK Hajduk and named after the hajduks, the outlaw heroes of Serbian epic poetry. After the Second World War the club played under several names before restoring the old one in 1949. Its home ground was the Stadion Milan Sredanović.

Hajduk won promotion to the Yugoslav top flight in 1991 and stayed there for 22 consecutive seasons, a run matched only by the country's biggest clubs. Backed for many years by the sponsor Rodić M&B, it finished fourth in the 1996–97 First League of FR Yugoslavia and again in the 2005–06 Serbia and Montenegro SuperLiga. That second fourth place took it into the 2006–07 UEFA Cup, where it went out to CSKA Sofia on away goals in the second qualifying round. The club also played in the Intertoto Cup in 1997 and 2007.

Financial problems grew after 2005, and on 30 July 2013, just before the new season, Hajduk withdrew from the SuperLiga and dissolved its first team. Successor clubs, OFK Hajduk and Hajduk Junior, have since carried on the name and symbols.

name: KSV Roeselare
content:
KSV Roeselare was a Belgian football club from the city of Roeselare in West Flanders. It traced its roots to SK Roeselare, founded in 1921 and registered with the matricule 134. In 1999 the club, then known as KSK Roeselare, merged with its local rival KFC Roeselare to form KSV Roeselare, which kept the number 134. Its home ground was the Schiervelde Stadion, which holds about 9,500 spectators.

In 2005 Roeselare won the Belgian Second Division final round, becoming the first club from the city to reach the top flight, where it stayed until 2010. In 2006 it took one of the extra UEFA Cup places awarded through the UEFA Fair Play ranking. In its only European campaign it beat Vardar in the first qualifying round before Ethnikos Achna knocked it out in the second.

After relegation the club spent a decade in the second tier, finishing runner-up in the First Division B in 2016–17. It later came under the ownership of Dai Yongge, ran into financial trouble, and was dissolved in 2020 after going bankrupt. A new club, SK Roeselare, was later set up in the city.

name: Empoli FC
content:
Empoli FC is an Italian professional football club from Empoli, a town in Tuscany between Florence and Pisa, founded in 1920. The club plays in blue and has its home at the Stadio Carlo Castellani, named after a former player who died in the Mauthausen concentration camp. It has been run for decades by president Fabrizio Corsi.

For most of its history Empoli played in the lower divisions, reaching Serie A for the first time in 1986. Since then it has moved regularly between Serie A and Serie B, earning a reputation as one of Italy's best talent factories and as a launch pad for coaches such as Luciano Spalletti, Maurizio Sarri and Marco Giampaolo.

Empoli's best Serie A finish, seventh place in 2006–07, took the club into Europe for the only time. In the 2007–08 UEFA Cup it beat FC Zürich 2–1 at home in the first round but lost the return leg 3–0 and went out.

name: FK Bežanija
content:
FK Bežanija is a Serbian football club from the Bežanija neighbourhood of New Belgrade, founded in 1921. In its early years it played under several names, including Soko, BSK and, during the Axis occupation, HŠK. After the Second World War it was called Jedinstvo, and it took the name Bežanija before the 1955–56 season. Its home ground is the small Stadion FK Bežanija.

The club rose through the lower leagues after the breakup of Yugoslavia and won the Serbian First League in 2005–06, earning a place in the new Serbian SuperLiga. It was the surprise of the league's first season in 2006–07, finishing fourth even though it had to play its home games at Železnik. That finish took Bežanija into the 2007–08 UEFA Cup, where it went out to Besa Kavajë in the first qualifying round on away goals without losing a match.

Bežanija was relegated in 2008 and then spent eleven seasons in the Serbian First League. Financial trouble forced it to withdraw in 2019, and it now plays in the lower tiers of Belgrade football.

name: FC Okzhetpes
content:
FC Okzhetpes is a Kazakh professional football club from Kokshetau in the north of the country, founded in 1957 as Torpedo. It takes its name from the Okzhetpes cliff in the nearby Burabay area, whose name means "an arrow won't reach". The club plays at the Torpedo Stadium in Kokshetau, which holds about 10,000 spectators.

Its history has been unusually restless. The club was renamed Spartak, Kokshetau, Kokshe, Avtomobilist, Khimik, Akmola and Esil, and in the late 1990s it briefly moved to Shortandy and then to Stepnogorsk before returning to Kokshetau in 2000. It has been known as Okzhetpes since 2004.

Although Okzhetpes finished only ninth in the 2008 Kazakhstan Premier League, it entered the first qualifying round of the inaugural 2009–10 UEFA Europa League because UEFA refused licences to higher-placed clubs and others withdrew. In that tie it won 2–1 away at Zimbru Chișinău but lost the return 2–0 at home. The club has since moved between the Premier League and the First Division.

name: Olympiacos Volos FC
content:
Olympiacos Volos is a Greek football club from the port city of Volos in Thessaly, founded on 2 June 1937. In 1961 it merged with local side Ethnikos Volos and played for decades as Ethnikos Olympiacos Volos, although it was always known simply as Olympiacos Volos. Its traditional colours are red and white, and it plays its home matches in Volos.

The club first reached the top flight in 1966 and then spent several spells moving between the first and second divisions until the late 1980s. Financial collapse in the early 2000s sent it down to the fourth tier, but it climbed back up and in 2010–11, after more than twenty years away, it finished fifth in the Super League.

That fifth place took Olympiacos Volos into the 2011–12 UEFA Europa League, where it beat Rad and Differdange 03 in the qualifying rounds. Before the play-off round, however, UEFA expelled the club for its involvement in the Koriopolis match-fixing scandal and gave its place to Differdange. The Greek federation also relegated the club, and it has since played in the regional and lower national divisions.

name: Levante UD
content:
Levante UD is a Spanish professional football club from Valencia, founded on 6 September 1909, which makes it the oldest club in the city. It plays in blue and red, and its supporters are known as the Granotes (the Frogs). The club plays its home matches at the Estadi Ciutat de València in the north of the city, which holds about 26,000 spectators.

Overshadowed for most of its history by its neighbour Valencia CF, Levante spent long periods in the second and third tiers. It won the Copa de la España Libre in 1937 and reached La Liga for the first time in 1963. Since the 2000s it has become a regular member of the top flight, though it has also been relegated several times.

Levante's best La Liga finish, sixth place in 2011–12, took the club into the 2012–13 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign so far. It came through the play-off round and the group stage and knocked out Olympiacos in the round of 32, before losing to Rubin Kazan after extra time in the round of 16.

name: IF Brommapojkarna
content:
IF Brommapojkarna, usually called BP, is a Swedish football club from the borough of Bromma in western Stockholm, founded on 13 April 1942. In its early years it also ran athletics, bandy and ice hockey sections. Its home ground is the Grimsta IP, which holds about 6,800 spectators.

BP is best known for its youth academy, said to be the largest in Europe by number of active youth teams. It has produced many Swedish internationals, among them John Guidetti, and has had partnership agreements with Manchester United and later Manchester City.

The men's team first reached the Allsvenskan in 2006 and has since moved several times between the top flight and the Superettan. In 2014 it entered the UEFA Europa League through the Fair Play ranking. It beat VPS and Crusaders in the first two qualifying rounds, playing its home matches at the Tele2 Arena, before Torino knocked it out in the third qualifying round.

name: Kardemir Karabükspor
content:
Kardemir Karabükspor was a Turkish football club from the steel town of Karabük, formed in 1969 by a merger of Karabük Gençlikspor and Demir Çelik Spor. It was named after Kardemir, the local iron and steel works, and its nickname, Mavi Ateş (Blue Flame), came from the blue flames of the factory chimneys. It played at the Dr. Necmettin Şeyhoğlu Stadium.

Karabükspor had spells in the Süper Lig in the 1990s and returned to the top flight in 2010 after eleven years away. In the 2014–15 UEFA Europa League it knocked out Rosenborg on away goals in the third qualifying round. It then beat Saint-Étienne 1–0 at home in the play-off round, but lost the return leg 1–0 and went out on penalties.

After relegation from the Süper Lig in 2018, the club collapsed financially and suffered several more relegations in a row. In 2022 it could not field a team and was dissolved. A successor club, Karabük İdman Yurdu, now uses its colours and plays at the same stadium.

name: FC Augsburg
content:
FC Augsburg is a German professional football club from Augsburg in Bavaria, founded on 8 August 1907 as FK Alemannia Augsburg. From 1921 to 1969 it played as BC Augsburg, and it took its present name in 1969 after a merger with TSV Schwaben Augsburg's football department. Since 2009 it has played at the WWK Arena south of the city centre, which holds about 30,600 spectators.

For most of its history the club moved between the second and third tiers, and in the early 2000s it even dropped to the fourth division for two seasons. It then recovered quickly, won promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2011, and has stayed in the top flight ever since.

Augsburg's fifth place in the 2014–15 Bundesliga took it into the 2015–16 UEFA Europa League, its first European campaign. It finished second in a group with Athletic Bilbao, Partizan and AZ, then lost narrowly to Liverpool in the round of 32 after a goalless first leg at home.

name: FC Botoșani
content:
FC Botoșani is a Romanian professional football club from Botoșani in the historical region of Moldavia, in the north-east of the country, founded in 2001. It plays in red, white and blue and has its home at the Botoșani Municipal Stadium, which holds about 7,800 spectators.

The club climbed through the lower divisions and won promotion to Liga I for the first time in 2013. Since then it has become an established member of the top flight, regularly finishing in the middle of the table.

Botoșani made its European debut in the 2015–16 UEFA Europa League, qualifying through the Fair Play ranking. It knocked out Georgia's Tskhinvali in the first qualifying round before Legia Warsaw eliminated it in the second.

name: FC Saksan
content:
FC Saksan, originally FC Saxan, is a Moldovan football club from Ceadîr-Lunga in the autonomous region of Gagauzia, founded in 2010. Its home ground is the small Ceadîr-Lunga Stadium. Since 2019 the club has been re-founded several times under the names CSCT Saksan and FC Saksan.

Saxan won the Divizia A, the Moldovan second tier, in 2013–14 and was promoted to the National Division, where it quickly established itself in the upper half of the table.

The club's only European campaign came in the 2015–16 UEFA Europa League, where Apollon Limassol knocked it out in the first qualifying round. Saxan played its home leg at the Zimbru Stadium in Chișinău. Financial problems later forced it out of the top flight.

name: FC Tskhinvali
content:
FC Tskhinvali was a Georgian football club named after the city of Tskhinvali in South Ossetia, founded in 1936 as Spartaki. It later played as Liakhvi and Tskhinvali before reverting to Spartaki in 2007 and taking the name Tskhinvali again in 2015.

Because of the Georgian–Ossetian conflict, the club could not play in Tskhinvali itself and hosted its matches in Georgian-controlled cities, mostly Gori, Tbilisi and Rustavi. In the mid-2010s it spent four seasons in the Georgian top flight.

Tskhinvali's only European appearance came in the 2015–16 UEFA Europa League, where FC Botoșani beat it in the first qualifying round, with the home leg played in Tbilisi. A severe financial crisis followed, and in early 2020 the club was disqualified from Liga 3 and dissolved.

name: Ankaraspor
content:
Ankaraspor is a Turkish football club from the capital Ankara, founded in 1978 as the club of the Ankara municipality. In the 2000s it reached the Süper Lig, but in 2009 it was relegated by the federation over its links with the city's other club, Ankaragücü, and it later had to be re-formed.

From 2014 to 2020 the club played as Osmanlıspor, at the Osmanlı Stadyumu in Ankara. Under that name it won promotion back to the Süper Lig and finished fifth in 2015–16, its best ever league position.

That fifth place took Osmanlıspor into the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign. It came through three qualifying rounds against Zimbru, Nõmme Kalju and Midtjylland, and then won a group containing Villarreal, Steaua and Zürich. Olympiacos knocked it out in the round of 32. The club reverted to the name Ankaraspor in 2020 and now plays in the lower divisions.

name: FC Arouca
content:
FC Arouca is a Portuguese football club from the small town of Arouca in the Porto metropolitan area, founded on 25 December 1951. It plays its home matches at the Estádio Municipal de Arouca, which holds about 5,600 spectators. Its supporters call the team the Lobos (Wolves).

For most of its history Arouca played in the regional and lower national leagues. It rose quickly through the divisions in the 2000s and reached the Primeira Liga for the first time in 2013.

In 2015–16 Arouca finished fifth, its best ever league position, and qualified for the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League. It knocked out Heracles Almelo on away goals in the third qualifying round, before losing to Olympiacos after extra time in the play-off round. After a spell back in the lower divisions, the club returned to the Primeira Liga and played in Europe again in 2022–23.

name: FC Politehnica Iași
content:
FC Politehnica Iași was a Romanian football club from Iași, the largest city in the Romanian part of Moldavia. It was founded in 2010 as CSM Politehnica Iași, taking over the tradition of the city's earlier Politehnica club, whose history went back to 1945. It played at the Emil Alexandrescu Stadium, which holds about 11,400 spectators.

Poli won promotion to Liga I in 2014 and finished sixth in the 2015–16 season. That result took it into the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League, where it drew 2–2 at home with Hajduk Split but lost the return 2–1 in Split and went out in the second qualifying round.

The club spent several more seasons in the top flight before financial problems took hold. It was dissolved in July 2026.

name: FK Bokelj
content:
FK Bokelj is a Montenegrin football club from the historic coastal town of Kotor on the Bay of Kotor, founded in 1922. Its home ground is the small Stadion Pod Vrmcem in Kotor. The club takes its name from the Bokelji, the people of the Bay of Kotor.

During the Yugoslav era Bokelj mostly played in the regional and second-tier leagues. After Montenegro's independence it has moved between the Montenegrin First and Second Leagues.

Bokelj's only European campaign came in the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League, which it entered as runner-up in the Montenegrin Cup. In the first qualifying round it drew 1–1 with Vojvodina at home, playing the match in Petrovac, but lost the return leg 5–0 in Novi Sad.

name: PAS Giannina FC
content:
PAS Giannina is a Greek football club from Ioannina, the capital of the Epirus region, founded on 8 July 1966 through the merger of several local clubs. It is the football section of the PAS Giannina multi-sport club and plays at the Zosimades Stadium, which holds about 7,600 spectators. Its blue and white colours earned it the nickname Ajax of Epirus.

PAS Giannina is the most successful club in Epirus and has spent many seasons in the Greek top flight since the 1970s, alternating with spells in the second tier.

In the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League, its first European campaign, it beat Odd in the second qualifying round after extra time and then lost narrowly to AZ in the third. It played that home tie at the Peristeri Stadium in Athens because the Zosimades did not meet UEFA criteria.

name: US Sassuolo Calcio
content:
US Sassuolo Calcio is an Italian professional football club from Sassuolo, a small town in Emilia-Romagna known for its ceramics industry. It was founded in 1920 and refounded as US Sassuolo in 1974. The team plays in black and green, which gives it the nickname Neroverdi, and has its home at the Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore in nearby Reggio Emilia.

Backed by the Mapei company and its owner Giorgio Squinzi, Sassuolo rose rapidly from the amateur leagues and reached Serie A for the first time in 2013. It soon became an established top-flight club known for attacking football and young Italian players.

Sassuolo's sixth place in 2015–16 took it into the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League, its first European campaign. It knocked out Luzern and Red Star Belgrade in the qualifying rounds, but finished third in a group with Genk, Athletic Bilbao and Rapid Wien.
stadium: Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore, Cap. 21,584

name: FC Olimpik Donetsk
content:
FC Olimpik Donetsk was a Ukrainian football club from Donetsk, founded in 2001. Its home was the small Sports Complex Olimpik in Donetsk, which holds about 3,000 spectators.

Olimpik climbed through the professional leagues and reached the Ukrainian Premier League in 2014, just as the war in Donbas began. Because of the conflict it never played a top-flight match in Donetsk and spent its Premier League years in Kyiv, with brief plans to move to Sumy or Cherkasy that came to nothing.

The club's best season was 2016–17, when it finished fifth and qualified for the 2017–18 UEFA Europa League. In the third qualifying round it drew 1–1 with PAOK in Kyiv but lost the return leg 2–0 in Thessaloniki. Olimpik stopped playing in 2022 after the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

name: FC Ufa
content:
FC Ufa is a Russian football club from Ufa, the capital of the Republic of Bashkortostan, founded on 23 December 2010. It plays at the Neftyanik Stadium, which holds about 15,000 spectators. Its nickname is Gorozhane (The Citizens).

Backed by the regional government, Ufa rose quickly through the Russian leagues and reached the Premier League for the first time in 2014, where it spent several seasons.

Ufa's sixth place in 2017–18 took it into the 2018–19 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign. It knocked out Domžale on away goals in the second qualifying round and then beat Progrès Niederkorn, before losing 2–1 on aggregate to Rangers in the play-off round. The club was later relegated and now plays in the Russian First League.

name: Cardiff Met FC
content:
Cardiff Met FC is the football club of Cardiff Metropolitan University, based at the university's Cyncoed campus in Cardiff. It was founded in 1957 and has played under several names linked to the institution, including Cardiff Metropolitan University FC. Its home ground is the Cyncoed Stadium, which holds about 1,600 spectators. The team is nicknamed The Archers, after the bowman on its badge.

Made up largely of students, the club climbed the Welsh pyramid and reached the Cymru Premier, the national top flight, in 2016. It quickly established itself there and won the Welsh League Cup in 2019.

That cup win, through a Cymru Premier play-off place, took the club into the preliminary round of the 2019–20 UEFA Europa League, its European debut. After losing 1–0 to Progrès Niederkorn in Luxembourg, it won the return leg 2–1 in Cardiff but went out on away goals.

name: FC Arsenal Tula
content:
FC Arsenal Tula is a Russian football club from Tula, the city south of Moscow known for its arms factories. The club traces its history to 1946 and has played under several names, adopting Arsenal, a nod to the city's gunsmithing tradition, in the 1990s. It plays at the Arsenal Stadium, which holds about 19,000 spectators.

Arsenal spent most of the Soviet and early Russian years in the lower divisions. It first reached the Russian Premier League in 2014 and, after several promotions and relegations, became a regular member of the top flight in the late 2010s.

Arsenal's sixth place in 2018–19 took it into the 2019–20 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign. Neftçi Baku knocked it out in the second qualifying round, winning 1–0 in Tula and 3–0 in Baku. The club was later relegated and now plays in the Russian First League.

name: CSF Speranța Nisporeni
content:
CSF Speranța Nisporeni was a Moldovan football club from the town of Nisporeni in the centre of the country, founded in 1991. It played at the Stadionul Mircea Eliade in Nisporeni, which held about 2,500 spectators.

The club spent most of its history in the lower divisions before reaching the National Division, Moldova's top flight, in the 2010s. Its best season came in 2018–19, when it reached the Moldovan Cup final and so earned a European place.

Speranța's only European campaign came in the 2019–20 UEFA Europa League, where Neftçi Baku knocked it out in the first qualifying round, winning 3–0 in Chișinău and 6–0 in Baku. The club ran into financial difficulties soon afterwards and was dissolved in 2021.

name: Yeni Malatyaspor
content:
Yeni Malatyaspor is a Turkish football club from Malatya in eastern Anatolia, founded in 1986 as Malatya Belediyespor, the club of the city municipality. It took its present name in 2010 and now plays at the New Malatya Stadium, which holds about 27,000 spectators.

The club rose rapidly through the Turkish leagues in the 2010s and reached the Süper Lig for the first time in 2017. In 2018–19 it finished fifth, its best ever league position.

That fifth place took Yeni Malatyaspor into the 2019–20 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign. It knocked out Olimpija Ljubljana in the second qualifying round, then lost to Partizan in the third despite winning the home leg 1–0. Partizan were later punished for racist behaviour by their supporters during the tie. After relegation in 2022 the club fell into financial crisis and dropped to the lower divisions.

name: FC Desna Chernihiv
content:
FC Desna Chernihiv is a Ukrainian football club from Chernihiv in the north of the country, founded in 1960 as Avanhard and named after the Desna river from 1961. In the Soviet era the club spent many years in the lower leagues, and for a period in the 1970s it was replaced by an army team that represented the city. Its home was the Chernihiv Stadium, named after Yuri Gagarin, which held about 12,000 spectators.

After Ukrainian independence Desna moved between the second and third tiers. It reached the Ukrainian Premier League for the first time in 2018, and in 2019–20 it finished fourth, its best ever result.

That fourth place took Desna into the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League, its only European campaign. Because of the pandemic, ties were single matches, and Desna lost 2–0 away to VfL Wolfsburg in the third qualifying round. In 2022 the Russian invasion devastated Chernihiv and damaged the club's stadium, and Desna stopped competing.

name: FC Dinamo-Auto Tiraspol
content:
FC Dinamo-Auto Tiraspol was a Moldovan football club named after Tiraspol but based in the village of Tîrnauca in Slobozia District, on the left bank of the Dniester, where it played at the small Dinamo-Auto Stadium. It was founded on 24 July 2009.

The club won promotion to the National Division in 2013 and became a regular member of the Moldovan top flight. A third-place finish in 2020 earned it a place in Europe.

Dinamo-Auto's only European campaign came in the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League, when, because of the pandemic, ties were single matches. It lost 2–1 away to Ventspils in the first qualifying round. The club was dissolved in 2024.

name: FC Kolos Kovalivka
content:
FC Kolos Kovalivka is a Ukrainian football club from the village of Kovalivka in Kyiv Oblast, founded in 2012. It plays in white and black at the Kolos Stadium in Kovalivka, which holds about 5,000 spectators. It is one of the few top-flight clubs in Europe based in a village.

Kolos rose from amateur football to the professional leagues within a few years and won promotion to the Ukrainian Premier League in June 2019. In its first top-flight season it finished fifth.

That fifth place took Kolos into the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League, its European debut, played as single matches because of the pandemic. It won 2–1 away to Aris in the second qualifying round, then lost 2–0 at Rijeka in the third.

name: Sirens FC
content:
Sirens FC is a Maltese football club from the seaside village of San Pawl il-Baħar (St. Paul's Bay) on the north-west coast of Malta, founded in 1968. Its small home ground, the Sirens Stadium, holds about 600 spectators, although like most Maltese clubs it plays its league matches at the country's shared stadiums.

For most of its history Sirens played in the lower divisions. It reached the Maltese Premier League in the late 2010s and soon established itself there.

Sirens made its European debut in the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League, when ties were single matches because of the pandemic. It lost narrowly, 2–1, to CSKA Sofia in Sofia in the first qualifying round.

name: Union Titus Pétange
content:
Union Titus Pétange is a Luxembourgish football club from Pétange in the south-west of the country. It was formed on 29 April 2015 through the merger of CS Pétange, founded in 1910, and FC Titus Lamadelaine. The club plays at the Stade Municipal in Pétange, which holds about 2,400 spectators.

Soon after the merger the club established itself in the National Division, Luxembourg's top flight. In 2019–20 it finished in a European place for the first time.

Union Titus Pétange made its European debut in the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League, played as single matches because of the pandemic, and lost 2–0 away to Lincoln Red Imps in Gibraltar in the first qualifying round. The club later dropped to the Division of Honour.

name: CD Santa Clara
content:
CD Santa Clara is a Portuguese professional football club from Ponta Delgada on São Miguel, the largest island of the Azores, founded in 1921. It plays at the Estádio de São Miguel, which holds about 12,500 spectators, and is known as Os Açorianos (The Azoreans). It is the most successful club from the archipelago.

Santa Clara first reached the Primeira Liga in 1999 and has since moved several times between the top two divisions. Its long trips to and from mainland Portugal have always been part of the club's identity.

Santa Clara's sixth place in 2020–21 took it into the first edition of the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2021–22, making it the first Azorean club to play in a UEFA club competition proper. It beat Shkupi and Olimpija Ljubljana before Partizan knocked it out in the play-off round.

name: FK Podgorica
content:
FK Podgorica is a Montenegrin football club from the south-western part of the capital, Podgorica, founded in 1970. For most of its history it was known as OFK Mladost 1970 (also Mladost Lješkopolje). After a period of inactivity the club was revived in 2014 and renamed FK Podgorica in 2019. It plays at the DG Arena, which holds about 4,000 spectators.

After its revival the club rose quickly through the Montenegrin leagues and reached the First League, where it soon competed near the top of the table.

FK Podgorica made its European debut in the first edition of the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2021–22. It beat Laçi 1–0 at home in the first qualifying round but lost the return 3–0 in Elbasan.

name: Mons Calpe SC
content:
Mons Calpe SC is a sports club from Gibraltar, founded in 2013 and named after the Latin name for the Rock of Gibraltar. Besides football it runs futsal and darts sections and an under-23 team. Like all Gibraltar clubs, it plays at the Victoria Stadium.

The club joined the Gibraltar football league system soon after its foundation and established itself in the Gibraltar Football League.

Mons Calpe's only European campaign came in the first edition of the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2021–22. It drew 1–1 at home with FC Santa Coloma in the first qualifying round, then lost the return leg 4–0 in Andorra.

name: Mosta FC
content:
Mosta FC is a Maltese football club from the town of Mosta in the centre of Malta, founded in 1935. Its small home ground is the Charles Abela Memorial Stadium in Mosta, although like most Maltese clubs it plays its league matches at the national stadiums. Its nickname is Il-Baqar.

Mosta has played in the Maltese Premier League since the 2011–12 season, mostly in the middle of the table.

Mosta made its European debut in the first edition of the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2021–22. It beat Spartak Trnava 3–2 at the Centenary Stadium in the first qualifying round, but lost the return 2–0 in Trnava and went out.

name: Gil Vicente FC
content:
Gil Vicente FC is a Portuguese professional football club from Barcelos in the north of the country, founded on 3 May 1924 and named after the Renaissance playwright Gil Vicente. It plays at the Estádio Cidade de Barcelos, which holds about 12,000 spectators. Its nicknames are Gilistas and Galos (Roosters), after the famous Rooster of Barcelos.

The club first reached the Primeira Liga in 1990 and has since spent many seasons in the top flight. In 2006 it was relegated administratively in the so-called Mateus case, and it returned to the top division in 2019 after a long legal dispute.

Gil Vicente's fifth place in 2021–22, its best ever league finish, took it into the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League, its European debut. It beat Riga 4–0 at home in the third qualifying round after a 1–1 draw away, then lost to AZ Alkmaar in the play-off round.

name: 1. FC Heidenheim
content:
1. FC Heidenheim 1846 is a German professional football club from Heidenheim an der Brenz in Baden-Württemberg. It traces its roots to a gymnastics club founded in 1846, which makes it the oldest professional football club in Germany. The present football club was formed in 1972 and plays at the Voith-Arena, which holds about 15,000 spectators.

Under long-serving coach Frank Schmidt, Heidenheim climbed from the regional leagues to the 2. Bundesliga in 2014. In 2023 it won promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time, and it finished eighth in its first top-flight season.

That eighth place took Heidenheim into the 2024–25 UEFA Conference League, its European debut. It beat BK Häcken in the play-off round and reached the knockout phase play-offs from the league phase, where Copenhagen knocked it out after extra time.

name: FK Radnički 1923
content:
FK Radnički 1923, historically known as Radnički Kragujevac, is a Serbian football club from Kragujevac in central Serbia, founded in 1923. It is the main part of the Radnički Kragujevac sports society and plays at the Čika Dača Stadium, which holds about 15,000 spectators. The stadium is named after Danilo Stojanović, who is said to have brought football to Serbia.

The club spent several seasons in the Yugoslav First League and later became a regular member of the Serbian top flight, the SuperLiga. A fourth-place finish in 2023–24 earned it a European place.

In the 2024–25 UEFA Conference League, its first European campaign since the Intertoto Cup era, Radnički beat Mornar 1–0 at home in the second qualifying round. It lost the return 2–1 in Podgorica and went out on penalties. The home leg was played in Leskovac.

name: BFC Daugavpils
content:
BFC Daugavpils is a Latvian football club from Daugavpils, the country's second-largest city, in the south-east near the borders with Lithuania and Belarus. It was founded on 11 December 2009 as BFC Daugava, a football centre that took over youth football in the city, and later adopted the name Daugavpils. It plays at the Esplanādes stadions, which holds about 700 spectators.

The club established itself in the Latvian Higher League in the 2010s and 2020s, carrying on the city's football tradition after the older clubs FC Daugava and Dinaburg had ceased to exist.

BFC Daugavpils made its European debut in the 2025–26 UEFA Conference League. It won 1–0 away to Vllaznia in the first qualifying round but lost the return leg 4–2 in Riga, where it played its home match, and went out.

name: MKT Araz FK
content:
MKT Araz FK was an Azerbaijani football club based in Imishli. It was founded in 2004 by MKT Istehsalat-Kommersiya, a cotton manufacturing company, which gave the team its nickname, Pambıqçılar (The Cottongrowers). The club was admitted straight to the Azerbaijan Top League and played at the Heydar Aliyev Stadium in Imishli, which opened in March 2006 and holds 8,500 spectators.

MKT Araz finished 8th in its first season and 9th in 2005–06. In 2006–07, its best season, it came 5th in the league and reached the final of the Azerbaijan Cup, where it lost 1–0 to Khazar Lankaran. Because Khazar also won the league, MKT Araz qualified for the 2007–08 UEFA Cup, where it went out in the first qualifying round to Dyskobolia Grodzisk Wielkopolski (0–0 at home and 0–1 away).

UEFA declared the club defunct in August 2007, and after that it dropped to the First Division and was dissolved several times. In 2013 it was re-established as Mil-Muğan FK and played in the First Division until it ceased to exist in 2018. In 2022 a new club, İmişli FK, was founded in the city and carries on its football tradition.
stadium: Heydar Aliyev – MKT Araz Stadium, Cap. 8,500
